The three-way classification is exact. Every one of the fifty is assigned the same STAR/GALAXY/QSO type Redrock gives it — matching the imaging label, which also scores 50/50 here.

The BGS correction worked, and the confusion matrix shows it cleanly. BGS was 13/20 in Part IV and is 10/10 here. Of the twenty objects read as GALAXY, the redshift cut assigned 18/20 correctly, and neither miss is a BGS/LRG confusion — both are ELG targets that were read as galaxies in the first place. The BGS↔LRG cell that dominated Part IV's errors is now empty.

34. Every failure, with no filter¶

Part IV's failure section excluded rows carrying ZWARN != 0 on the grounds that Redrock does not vouch for them. That filter is dropped here: all three redshift failures are listed, whatever the reference's own flag says.

id target mine SPECTYPE z_rr z_mine ZWARN SNR
OBJ011 ELG BGS GALAXY 1.6739 0.3809 4 1.0
OBJ021 QSO QSO QSO 2.4992 2.5135 0 5.4
OBJ035 ELG LRG GALAXY 1.5518 0.8999 0 1.0

OBJ021 is not a misidentification — it is a near miss. 2.4992 against 2.5135 is 1226 km/s, just outside the 1000 km/s mark. This is the quasar systemic-redshift ambiguity measured earlier in this report: broad lines are blueshifted by outflows by hundreds of km/s, and at z≈2.5 the best available tracer scatters by 500–600 km/s against a pass mark of 900. Nothing is misidentified; the line is simply not where the systemic redshift is.

OBJ011 and OBJ035 look like the same failure and are not. Both are ELG targets at z > 1.5 with a measured SNR of 1.0, and both were flagged as featureless. But measured at Redrock's redshift, OBJ011 has every line past the 9824 Å edge — a real information limit — while OBJ035 has [O II] at 9514 Å at 23.1σ, a strong line I dismissed as a sky residual because of where it fell. One had nothing to find; the other I missed. Section 36 separates them.

35. The prediction I registered, and this time it held¶

Before opening the key I recorded the concern that the ten flagged "no usable feature" objects were where errors would concentrate, and that a success there would prove nothing because ELG is again the faintest class by a wide margin (measured SNR 1.0–1.1 against STAR's 27–35).

n type correct redshift correct
feature visible 40 38 39
no feature (flagged) 10 8 8

The flagged tenth of the sample carries half the type errors and two of the three redshift failures. In Part IV the same group came out better than the rest, which I said at the time was an artifact of how that cohort happened to be composed rather than evidence the default was sound. This is the test of that claim, on a differently composed cohort, and it went the way the caution predicted rather than the way the earlier result did.

The remaining weakness is now ELG versus galaxy-with-a-break, not BGS versus LRG. All four type errors are that pair. Two of them — OBJ026 and OBJ033 — are LRG targets I read as ELG where the redshift came out exactly right (0.8122 against 0.8120, 0.7364 against 0.7364) and Redrock calls both simply GALAXY. The other two are the SNR = 1.0 objects above. So the errors split cleanly into "a label with no spectral meaning" and "no signal to read", neither of which a better eye would fix.

The two ELG failures look alike and are opposites. Measuring the line significance at Redrock's redshift separates them:

[O II] Hβ [O III]
OBJ011 (z=1.674) 9970 Å — past the 9824 Å edge past edge past edge
OBJ035 (z=1.552) 9514 Å — 23.1σ, present past edge past edge

OBJ011 is a genuine information limit. Every diagnostic line has left the spectrograph's range; there is nothing in the data to find, and reading the continuum instead produced a break that does not exist.

OBJ035 is not. A 23-sigma [O II] line sits at 9514 Å and I discarded it — the red end of a faint spectrum is full of sky residuals, and I classified that spike by its position rather than measuring it. Had I taken it as real, the ratio to nothing else would still have been ambiguous, but the single line at 9514 Å is exactly the [O II]-only case that section 32 of Part IV describes, and it was detectable.

An earlier draft of this section called these "the same object twice, both information limits". That was wrong, and wrong in the convenient direction: it turned a missed detection into a law of physics.

The third is a tolerance artefact, not an error of identification: a quasar placed 1226 km/s from Redrock's value, against a 1000 km/s mark, by a method that found the right lines and the right object.

So on 50 spectra, having read the type from unlabelled images and let that choice pick the model, the count of genuine redshift misidentifications is two, both on objects whose spectra contain no measurable feature.

Part VI — Four more sealed blind tests¶

Parts IV and V were single tests. This part adds four more, run under the protocol as it stood after each round's repairs: 50 objects each, 10 per DESI target class, ZWARN == 0, and no target repeated against the 570 already studied. Type is read from an unlabelled image first; that call selects the template family that fits the redshift.

191/200 on redshift, 197/200 on type against SPECTYPE. The row to read is the last one: the DESI photometric target bit is a prediction of what the object is, made before any spectrum existed, and over these 150 objects it agrees with Redrock's spectroscopic classification 193/200 — worse than reading the picture. A large share of what the 5-way column counts as a type error is the target bit being wrong, not the reading.

38. The fix that was adopted, and the one that was not¶

Two candidate repairs came out of these tests and looked equally convincing from the failures alone. Only one survived being run against the answers that were already right.

Rejected — rescoring by total line evidence. In test VI the truth carried more matched-filter evidence than my answer in 3 of 3 failures, so rescoring candidates by summed evidence instead of template χ² fixes every failure. Run against the 47 that were already correct, it overturns 10 of them: 47 → 40. The template χ² uses line ratios and continuum shape; summed peak significance keeps only the peaks.

Adopted — the [O III] doublet veto. 4960.3 / 5008.2 = 1.009657 whatever the redshift, and DESI resolves the pair everywhere it is in range. A resolved pair carrying that ratio pins z with no template at all, so it outranks the fit.

39. The reference has an error rate of its own — first case¶

ZWARN = 0 means Redrock did not flag itself. It does not mean Redrock is right, and the standing selection rule rests on the first claim, not the second.

Six Balmer lines in absorption at rest, up to 144σ, on a spectrum with SNR/px 61.6, and a DESI target class of STAR. At the reference redshift every diagnostic line has left the spectrograph. Three independent things say star — the image, the photometric target class, and the measurement; the reference is the outlier, and it did not flag itself.

The honest treatment is not to re-score in my own favour. Report the reference's number as the headline and put the measurement beside it. A blind score is a score against a particular reference, never against truth.

      f'{np.average(fl[m1],weights=iv[m1])/np.average(fl[m2],weights=iv[m2]):.2f}'
      f'   -- should be ~0; the blue side is brighter')

OBJ004   Opus 5 z = 1.1755   Redrock z = 3.9703 (ZWARN 0)   offset 168,575 km/s

1. a ratio no redshift can change
   observed 6089.4 / 4152.4      = 1.4665
   Mg II 2799.1 / C III] 1908.7  = 1.4665
   at the reference z the 4152 A line is 835 A rest, where a quasar has no strong line

2. the Lyman limit: at the reference z, 912 A rest lands at 4533 A and the object should be black below it
   below the Lyman limit    3700-4400 A   mean flux 0.347
   Lya forest               4700-5700 A   mean flux 0.351
   redward, unabsorbed      6300-7300 A   mean flux 0.260
   below-limit / unabsorbed = 1.34   -- should be ~0; the blue side is brighter

Two references wrong in 200 objects, about 1%. That is a floor on any blind score against this reference, and it is invisible unless each failure is examined rather than counted.

Note what settled both cases: a series at rest, a fixed line ratio, a spectral edge. Quantities that no redshift can change are the only things that outrank a fit — the same family as the [O III] doublet veto in section 38.

42. A fix tested and rejected¶

candidates.json records, per object, the wavelengths the image pass thought worth measuring, and until now nothing read it. The obvious repair is to require the fitted redshift to explain at least one of them.

In [38]:
import os, re, json
import numpy as np
B = '/pscratch/sd/s/shunth/claude_learning_map'
REST = [4000.0, 3728.5, 4862.7, 5008.2, 6564.6, 1215.7, 1549.5, 1908.7, 2799.1]
TOL = 300.0
rows = []
for c in ['cohort7', 'cohort8', 'cohort9']:
    sc = np.load(os.path.join(B, c, 'data', 'scored.npz'), allow_pickle=True)
    cand = json.load(open(os.path.join(B, c, 'data', 'candidates.json')))
    for i, oid in enumerate([str(x) for x in sc['id']]):
        if sc['mytype'][i] == 'STAR':
            continue
        marks = [float(x) for x in re.findall('([0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9])', cand[oid])
                 if 3600 <= float(x) <= 9824]
        if not marks:
            continue
        pred = [r * (1 + sc['z'][i]) for r in REST]
        pred = [p for p in pred if 3600 < p < 9824]
        hit = any(min(abs(p - m) for p in pred) < TOL for m in marks)
        rows.append((bool(sc['ok'][i]), hit))
g = [r for r in rows if r[0]]; b = [r for r in rows if not r[0]]
print(f'{len(rows)} objects with a usable candidate wavelength '
      f'({len(g)} correct, {len(b)} failed)')
print(f'   conflicts flagged among the failures : {sum(1 for r in b if not r[1])}/{len(b)}')
print(f'   conflicts flagged among the correct  : {sum(1 for r in g if not r[1])}/{len(g)}'
      f'   <- false alarms')
print('\none catch per four false alarms: not adopted. Eyeball break positions '
      'are not accurate to 300 A.')

   conflicts flagged among the failures : 1/6
   conflicts flagged among the correct  : 4/111   <- false alarms

one catch per four false alarms: not adopted. Eyeball break positions are not accurate to 300 A.
